utterances.text: Yes but at the moment I can't remember. I may have signed a record, if a record was made, but I can't tell you for sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Witness, have you yourself seen a certain number of these forms that had been filled in and that were returned to your department; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: SMAIL CEKIC
utterances.text: You mean returned by the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, no. Returned from the persons who were questioned or by the investigators.

utterances.speaker: SMAIL CEKIC
utterances.text: And you are asking me whether I saw those documents?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: SMAIL CEKIC
utterances.text: Yes. On a daily basis I would see these documents on a daily basis because I have access to the documents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So could you confirm to this Trial Chamber that with regard to these two headings that we are talking about, wounds and people killed, could you say that -- could you say that in general the street and the number of the street where the incident occurred is not mentioned?

utterances.speaker: SMAIL CEKIC
utterances.text: I can't answer that question with certainty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: SMAIL CEKIC
utterances.text: Because the analytic processing of this information has not yet been completed and this is a task that we must still complete.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Witness, I realise that there was a committee that decided on the elaboration of this questionnaire. With regard to the wounded and dead, during the period of what you just called "aggression" did someone within this community ever think of including a heading which would allow one to know and I think that this is something that is necessary, whether the incident occurred near the front line or near a military target; yes or no, if you can answer that question.

utterances.speaker: SMAIL CEKIC
utterances.text: Sir, this questionnaire which was compiled at the time when a scientific team existed, all of your comments which relate to the contents of this questionnaire, right now at this moment, they can't be a subject of discussion because the questionnaire such as it is was compiled at the time. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, I understand you very well. But do you know, yes or no, whether this question was elaborated? If you don't know, just say that you don't know.

utterances.speaker: SMAIL CEKIC
utterances.text: No, I am not aware of this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Witness, as director of the institute, do you know whether one thought of including a heading for these two parts regarding the existence at the time of the incident, of fighting that might have been ongoing in or -- in Sarajevo or in the surroundings of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: SMAIL CEKIC
utterances.text: Military questions -- this questionnaire didn't deal with military questions to the extent that you are insisting on. But as part of this entire project, there are studies which are being carried out. And in those studies this is -- will be addressed too, but that research has not yet been completed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Witness, I see that you are taking notes is this to make a report to someone or is this because you need them in order to answer questions.

utterances.speaker: SMAIL CEKIC
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, this is how I usually work. I can concentrate far better if I do this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. So take the following note, please --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, there is no way of you telling what notes the witness should take. You can ask --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you very much. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do the following names, are they familiar to you: Silos, Sunce, Viktor Bubanj, Borcelino, Pazaric, and Hrasnica?

utterances.speaker: SMAIL CEKIC
utterances.text: Could you please repeat that if it's not too difficult. Could you please repeat the names?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It hasn't been noted, this is why I wanted you to take notes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Cekic, I think Mr. Piletta-Zanin would like to know whether the names he uses -- he mentions do ring a bell to you. Would you please, one by one, give the names, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Willingly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Silos, Sunce --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps, Mr. Witness, if they do ring a bell if not, just say no.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The first name is particular to me. Sunce isn't. Carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, what is Silos, please?

utterances.speaker: SMAIL CEKIC
utterances.text: Up until the current state of investigation, within the project of victims in Sarajevo, within this project, one will also address the issue of Serbian casualties in the area of the municipality which is called Hrasnica we dispose of certain information at this stage, according to which in the area of that municipality, certain crimes against Serbs were perpetrated. As to the extent of those crimes, this is a subject we can't discuss at the moment, but on the basis of this project, and 30 to 50 studies are planned as parts of this project, this issue is one that is going to be investigated too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. But, Witness, my question was, what is Silos?

utterances.speaker: SMAIL CEKIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, Silos is a location in the area of that municipality. It is a feature where as I said, according to the information we have at the moment, Serbs were victims there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Is that -- is it a camp?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I remind you that you have five minutes left.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it a camp?

utterances.speaker: SMAIL CEKIC
utterances.text: I apologise. Could you repeat that? Given that it is a scientific investigation, since this hasn't been investigated at the moment, I cannot tell you whether it is a camp or a prison. But I would like to remind you of the following fact: In some studies carried out today, with regards to camps, prisons, there is a lot of information and many authors often confuse those terms. They confuse prisons and camps, et cetera, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I apologise for interrupting you but we are short of time. Another name Viktor Bubanj, does this mean anything to you?

utterances.speaker: SMAIL CEKIC
utterances.text: Viktor Bubanj is the name of the -- of a JNA barracks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Do you know whether it is a prison or not?

utterances.speaker: SMAIL CEKIC
utterances.text: Once again, let me say that according to the information that we have at the moment --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you don't know, say no, we are short of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would ask you to slow down, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, because not only the interpreters but the court reporters have some difficulties. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Another name, Borsalino, does this mean anything to you?

utterances.speaker: SMAIL CEKIC
utterances.text: Borsalino, no, that doesn't mean anything to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Pazaric?

utterances.speaker: SMAIL CEKIC
utterances.text: Pazaric I know there is a place called like that in the surroundings of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it a name that corresponds to something in your investigation?

utterances.speaker: SMAIL CEKIC
utterances.text: Our investigation, the one that we carried out in 1994, doesn't cover that area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. What about Hrasnica? Was there a prison there?

utterances.speaker: SMAIL CEKIC
utterances.text: Hrasnica is a local commune which belonged to the municipality called Ilidza.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. But was there a prison there or not?

utterances.speaker: SMAIL CEKIC
utterances.text: I can't answer that question, I really can't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With the assistance of Madam Registrar and with your permission, Mr. President, I have one document that I would like to present, P3681, I would like the witness to be shown this exhibit and with your permission, I will ask a question about this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... having this document, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, how many Serb victims were there in Kazani, as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: SMAIL CEKIC
utterances.text: The investigating team of the institute is aware of the fact that at that spot a certain number of Serbs were the victims and that the authorities of Bosnia-Herzegovina, that is to say, the state Prosecutor in Sarajevo started proceedings, organised a trial, and that certain individuals were punished, the individuals who participated in those crimes. However, as to the number, I was getting there --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I will allow you, since the document is now there, to put one question to that, but time is over.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, could you please reply to me if you do know this, how many victims were there at Kazani? If you don't know, just simply say no, but if you do know, give us a figure.

utterances.speaker: SMAIL CEKIC
utterances.text: What I know, both as a scientist and as a person, as a human being, is that crimes were perpetrated there. However, I really and truly can't give you an answer as to the exact number of the Serbs killed there. This really large-scale project of ours will have to, and I stress, will have to provide an answer to that question by establishing names and surnames of all the victims.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That was your last question. And I explained that it is entirely up to the Defence whether they want to use that time to put questions on barricades or whatever, but one hour and a half is one hour and a half. Mr. Stamp is there -- no questions. Yes. Re-examined by Mr. Stamp:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were asked some questions about the vagueness of the questionnaire in respect to the place of event, place of event where the person was killed or injured. In the statement before the Court, you have said that the researchers of various backgrounds and balanced ethnicities from the civil protection staff completed these questionnaires by interviewing the various households in accordance with guidelines which were handed out. And I would like to show you one of the guidelines which is attached to your statement, if you would care to look at it? It is a document entitled, and you would have to forgive my pronunciation --

utterances.speaker: SMAIL CEKIC
utterances.text: What is the date that you are referring to? Perhaps it might speed things up

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Page 14, I take it, Mr. Stamp, on the bottom.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, page 14.

utterances.speaker: SMAIL CEKIC
utterances.text: 14. Just a second. I would find it easier if you were to tell me -- no, no, no. Page 14.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... perhaps if the usher could assist --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Looking at the bottom of the pages.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, does paragraph 5 in those guidelines give instructions in respect to obtaining information in respect to the place of events, that is the place where persons are killed, are killed or injured?

utterances.speaker: SMAIL CEKIC
utterances.text: Yes, you are right. In those cases in which we did have the information we should have stated the street and the address, well, this is indicated correctly. Thank you very much. You have noticed this and I thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: That will be all, Mr. President, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Cekic, since the Chamber has no further questions to you, this concludes your examination in this court. I would like to thank you very much for having come to The Hague. We all are aware that it is quite a journey and that you have answered the questions of the Defence and also one question of the Prosecution. Thank you very much. And I hope that you have a safe trip home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you and I wish all the best in your work to all of you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for that. Mr. Usher, could you please escort Mr. Cekic out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, perhaps first I give you another decision that is that the -- no, perhaps first I will ask you, you have filed the statement of the witness Cekic, and he has been cross-examined and I now see that we have a P-Exhibit which I take it contains exactly the same as was filed before?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, perhaps I -- I think we could admit it into evidence as a document in order to, but it is all the same, as far as I could see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, taking that it is exactly the same it has been filed, and there is the decision of the Chamber that this statement is admitted into evidence under Rule 92 bis. So if it's the same material, there's no use of tendering it anymore as a P Exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: These documents had been given to the court just out of convenience because it was five binders.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I've got two copies now. Thank you very much. Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: There was a matter I wanted the Court to find it convenient to deal with it now. The Court had ordered earlier today that a document of received evidence provided an official translation was made available and we would profit to the court, that translation P3748.1 and ask that it be received in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It says draft translation. But may I take it, that whether the word gives excellent opportunity to -- if I show it to you, you could even read it from that distance.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, it does, but I did ask that it be checked and this was the quickest way we could get it before the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but maybe we receive a confirmation from you by tomorrow that this is the translation and not a draft translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So that we are very sure about that. Then I give you another decision. All the documents tendered in relation to Witness AK are admitted into evidence, all of them under seal. Then, may I ask one question to the Prosecution: It was indicated that legal material -- no, we should not deal with that in open court. But some legal material was announced to be submitted which the Chamber did not receive until now. It is a matter that has been dealt with in closed session. If you do not understand what I mean, Mr. Ierace, we have to turn in closed session.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I understand, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and it is correct that we did not receive any material yet? You announced that you would submit legal materials, and until now, I haven't seen anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Perhaps I don't understand, Mr. President. Perhaps we can go into private session just for a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we will do that just for a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Meanwhile, we gave a decision in your absence, Mr. Ierace on 92 bis statement of Mr. Lesic which was not admitted into evidence. At this very moment, is the Prosecution ready to call its next witness, expert witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Before I do that, two matters. Do you envisage that the reasons for the decision will be published tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I hope so. The written decision is in preparation at this moment and we had a lot of decisions to take to.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, I appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- the last couple of days. So we do whatever we can and even if not the final written decision would be ready, we might already give you a part of the reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please authorise me to leave and I will come back as soon as possible, together with our expert.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And is then the Prosecution ready to call its next expert witness. Would you then, please, Mr. Usher, escort the witness into the courtroom. That would be Mr. Hinchliffe, as far as I understand. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon. I apologise for letting you wait for a second. Mr. Hinchliffe I presume --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sir, I can't hear you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, my first question is whether you can hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before giving testimony in this court -- yes, please. Before giving testimony in this court, Mr. Hinchliffe, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require you to make a solemn declaration that you will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth. May I invite you to make that declaration of which the text will now be handed out to you by the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Hinchliffe. Please be seated. Mr. Ierace, as the Chamber indicated before, that after a first short introduction, it might be that we would have some specific questions already for the expert witness. I would suggest that you examine the witness in perhaps in rather general terms and then we will see how we start tomorrow. Because there is 17 minutes left. Perhaps that might do for this first part of your examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Certainly, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have half an hour. We can go on until 5.15. Please proceed. Examined by Mr. Ierace:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your full name is Jonathan Paul Hinchliffe is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are a Captain in the British Army?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And indeed you are the officer commanding the sniper division of the British army is that so?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFF
utterances.text: Yes

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would like the witness to site a copy of this report which is P3740. I have some copies here if Madam Registrar does not have some.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: For those who have left them on their desk we have at least -- does the witness have the report? Or not yet?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is my report, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that your own copy is that the copy that was just given to you? Would you please look at the document now being presented to you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Hinchliffe, do you have before you a photocopy of your report dated the 4th of May 2002, and signed on the last page?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFF
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand that you want to make two corrections to the contents of that report. Is the first correction in relation to the type of weaponry which you say was used during the conflict?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFF
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please indicate what page and paragraph the first reference to that weapon appears.

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFF
utterances.text: I believe it is page 3, paragraph 12, under the heading of "equipment."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is that five lines down? Three lines down, I should say?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please read out the reference that you wish to change.

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFF
utterances.text: Where it is stated the sniper rifle use M 79, this should be deleted and insert M-76.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And does the second --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I ask one additional question. On the third line it says M-79 but it also on the 5th line, should it be changed there as well?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, perhaps I could assist.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does every reference to M-79 in the report should each such reference now read M-76

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, does the second change relate to the last sentence on that page which presently reads: "The Dragonov is a 6 times magnified sniper scope"?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What should that read?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFF
utterances.text: Times 4.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Times 4, all right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A semi-objection. Since you were moving rather swiftly and replies came rather fast, I couldn't follow. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then please proceed in a proper base, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I will, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us what information you used in the preparation of your report?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFF
utterances.text: I used information from my own experience and taken from infantry, from our weaponry books, which are on general release.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, you told us in the report that you travelled twice to Sarajevo as part of the preparation of it and that you were accompanied by various investigators from the Tribunal. In particular, to each site that you visited, did they provide you any information in terms of the evidence as they understood it?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFF
utterances.text: Yes they did. They explained quite clearly what the witnesses had stated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you visited each site did you locate a yellow marker in the form of a cross or a yellow post or similar object or marking?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFF
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, apart from the explanations given to you by the investigators on site, were you given any other material?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were you given?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFF
utterances.text: A brief description and the witness report of each incident.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say a "brief description" you understand that to be the contents of the first schedule to the indictment?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And indeed do you have a copy of that with you?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFF
utterances.text: I do indeed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also said that you were given a witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I will never be able to make my comments about the translation in writing as I am used to doing if you move this swiftly. If you don't want me to do it, I won't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I understand that you were asked to slow down. Would you please take that into consideration, Mr. Ierace. May I also ask you, to wait to answer the question until the cursor stops moving on your screen. Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you were also given a witness report of each incident. Did you use any of that information in the preparation of your report?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you use from the witness report or witness reports?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFF
utterances.text: I used the witness reports just to familiarise myself with the incidents and as well the direction of where they heard the shot and of specific matters, for example, the amount of bullets which were used.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say witness -- I withdraw that. Were you given any witness statements?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And did you use the contents of any witness statements in the preparation of your report?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you used the witness reports in order to familiarise the direction of where they heard the shot. Who do you mean by "they"?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFF
utterances.text: I mean the --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, since my learned colleague has made a distinction -- I do apologise. Since my learned colleague has made a distinction between a certain report and the statements, I would have liked him to specify just so as to make everything quite clear, whether he was referring to the statements or perhaps a possible other report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Mr. Ierace, you used both statements and witness reports. Would you please clarify or rephrase your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I would be happy to clarify it, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you mean two different types of documents when you referred to a witness report and a witness statement, or do you mean the same type of document?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFF
utterances.text: It was on one document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you given any documents which appeared to be an account by a witness of what they saw and what they heard, perhaps a page or two or three pages written in the first person or expressed in the first person and with their signature at the bottom of -- at the end of the document?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And when I use the term "witness statement" please understand that is what I am referring to. Now, separate from that type of document, were you given other documents of a different type?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFF
utterances.text: I was given that document and the first schedule of the indictments, which I based my information around.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "that document" you mean witness statements?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, were you shown any other types of documents apart from statements by witnesses?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFF
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the form of reports and tables and that sort of thing?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFF
utterances.text: Yes, I received an incident -- a document on each incident.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's call them "incident reports." Did you receive a number of those?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you use any of the information in the incident reports in your report to the Tribunal or not?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFF
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, over the last few days, have you been shown a video of each of the scheduled incidents, that is the incidents scheduled to the indictment except for scheduled incidents numbers 9 and 26?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you also been shown over that period of time 360 degree computerised photographs for each of those incidents, that is the scheduled incidents except for scheduled incident number 26?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President I would like to raise an objection here which is of a technical nature, in relation to this question for the simple reason that the Prosecution has indicated to us that these photos I believe, were not correct in terms of the way in which the data were calculated by the GPS device and asking a question about a piece of equipment with reference to which we were given to understand that it was imperfect, well it doesn't seem appropriate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When looking at the videos, did you pay specific attention to the GPS positions indicated on these videos?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think under these circumstances, Mr. Ierace could continue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Indeed, when you travelled to each of the sites and as you told us, located the yellow markers, did you do that with the assistance of GPS readings or the investigators or what?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFF
utterances.text: Investigator took me to each site and positioned me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in your report you expressed some opinions in relation to the strategy which you applied to the Serb forces. Have you any experience or other expertise in relation to determining the strategic use of snipers?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFF
utterances.text: Yes. I wrote the tactical doctrine and instituted plan for the British Army on how to use snipers. And I command the only course which teaches the employment of snipers around the battlefield and all phases of war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say that the course you run teaches the use of snipers in the battlefield who are the students of that course? What position do they told in relation to the snipers themselves?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFF
utterances.text: The students who attend the course are commanders of all levels from a section commander which is a corporal to captains and majors in the class.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now you also refer in your report to distances between where the alleged victims were shot and what we might call suspected sources of fire. In that regard, you tell us that you used a piece of equipment of a lighter brand I think it was laser, that appears on page 3 of your Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. report, at paragraph 13, you describe it as a leica vector, 1507 times 42 laser range finder. Can you give us some idea of the accuracy that that machine operates to?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFF
utterances.text: The leica vector 1500 will give you a range indication, a distance, plus or minus 3 metres up to 1.500 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And perhaps you could briefly explain to us in just a few sentences, if it can be done, how you operate such a piece of machinery or equipment in order to get a distance?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFF
utterances.text: The laser range finder is a hand held device, styled around a binocular instrument, you look through the laser range finder, position whatever target you are looking at, press a button which then fires a laser on to that target which is indicated by a red square, a small red square, and then after you release the button, the range is given in the bottom right-hand corner.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you recorded the -- I am sorry. When you operated the equipment and obtained the distances, did you record them in some fashion on site?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFF
utterances.text: I did. I recorded them in my notebook.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you prepared your report, did you have access to your notebook in order to ensure that the distances in the report were those that you recorded?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFF
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, they -- that concludes the questions that go to the qualifying of the witness. If the Bench has any enduring concerns, remaining concerns, would that be a convenient time for questions to be put to the witness from the Bench.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I will just consult with my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hinchliffe, I would like to ask you a few questions on your report. May I first draw your attention to serial 26. You write down in your report, "the firer observed a tiny light source." What makes you believe that the firer observed such a light source?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFF
utterances.text: When I was taken to this site and explained verbally, I was told the actual victim witness, one or the two, had indicated that a light source had been seen. Also, the incident happened during dark hours and the lights could be seen through the apartment windows.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What makes you draw such a conclusion. Let's just assume that the sniper would like to hit the next door apartment but missed it. What makes you believe that it was specifically this tiny light source that guided him?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFF
utterances.text: At a distance of 352 metres, estimated distance, a sniper would hit the target without missing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you would say if he is a good sniper, and if he targeted this flat, he should not have missed it.

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFF
utterances.text: At that distance, he would not have missed

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If he was a bit drunk --

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFF
utterances.text: He still would not have missed it. It is far too close.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you say, even drunk, you would not miss your target?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFF
utterances.text: I would say so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me ask you another question. Let me take you to serial 5. Where you conclude that it was a deliberate sniper shot, but you say "the firer was not particularly skilled. He underestimated the distance to his target from the fire position, which led to the bullet bouncing under the barricades and hitting the victim by pure chance." What is the basis for this conclusion?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFF
utterances.text: I assessed the situation, the incident, the firer to be at the top or near to the top of a building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What makes you believe that?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFF
utterances.text: That was pointed out to me by the investigator.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you say the investigator told me where the sniper was --

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFF
utterances.text: Where the sound was heard from and upon inspecting the building that he pointed to and at the top or near to the top, there was firing loop holes, several of them. A firing loop hole is where a single brick is removed and overlooking a certain area. You fire on to -- you fire through that hole.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you are telling us that it is very likely that the sniper shot from that position because that was an excellent position-- was an excellent opportunity to do that through this brick taken out.

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFF
utterances.text: Yes

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could he have fired from another place well let's say from a brick that was later placed back.

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFF
utterances.text: He could have. However, the situation that the investigator indicated to me is that it was from that position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If -- let me just assume that the sniper was using his weapon just because he wanted to hit something and not a specific person just to use it, what makes you draw the conclusion that the -- no, let me just first ask another question to you. You said the firer removed a brick and fired through the loop hole. What makes you believe that it was the firer that removed the brick? Could it have been one of his colleagues? Could it have been the previous owners of that apartment?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFF
utterances.text: That is possible. I know it is a common sniper practice to use that technique.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But your report says that the firer removed a brick.

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFF
utterances.text: Yes, I made that assessment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then you say in serial 5 "when the bullet was released from the firer, it was aimed precisely at the target." What makes you conclude that the bullet was released from the firer with aimed precision?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFF
utterances.text: From where the bullet was released and bounced to hit the individual, this suggested to me that the individual had been in the optical site picture of the sniper, however, the sniper had not understood the range from him to the individual properly. And therefore had got shot because -- bounced forward.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What is the methodology in which you used in order to reach these conclusions?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFF
utterances.text: The firer was shooting from a building, and as I assessed, a quite high up building, therefore it was an angled shot. This angled shot is a rather difficult shot because the weapon system believes that the system is on the ground, and therefore, the trajectory of the bullet would be incorrect if you are high up in a building. Therefore, you have to -- you can't just estimate from your position to the actual intended objective target. You have to use calculations to understand to reduce the actual angle and range.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I take you to serial 7. You say "the bullet fired entered the victim in the head. The shot was taken from a telescopic site." On what basis do you draw that conclusion?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFF
utterances.text: That assessment is made with from basically a bullet entering a person's head at such distance, as I estimated, would have to be an aimed shot in all probability. Therefore, I understood it to be an aimed shot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But on what -- on the basis -- I mean, if just a stray bullet would hit someone in his head --

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFF
utterances.text: That is possible. That is possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Even without a telescopic site?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFF
utterances.text: Yes. Celebrative fire or of some other means, however, I did assess this to be an aimed shot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: On serial 23 you write the following: "The firer engaged the victim at a minimum range of 560 metres. The fire position is unclear, however the front lines were situated so that the nearest building was 560 metres away." On the basis of what did you conclude that, although the fire position was unclear, that it was made from a building?

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFF
utterances.text: In my experience, a sniper would not want to expose himself in an open ground, be it from air, helicopters, airplane, or even artillery shells. A sniper is usually counter-sniped by indirect fire, artillery or mortar shelling. Therefore, if he is in a building, he has some defence above him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You say, "a single bullet at short distance engaged the victim therefore the fire was not well trained and probably in position of a hunting rifle with a poor sighting system." It is assessed the fire failed to kill the victim because he was inexperienced. If I would assume that this person using a hunting rifle or whatever other kind of weapon, had the intention to injure his victim rather than to kill him, what could you tell us about your conclusion that he failed to kill the victim because he was inexperienced.

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFF
utterances.text: This incident where the couple were walking away with their backs to the front lines, I assessed this incident that you would not release a bullet -- you intended to kill.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What if you want to injure someone.

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFF
utterances.text: I would assess the situation that there is no point injuring somebody, if you truly wanted to shoot, then you could shoot to kill.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: On the basis of what do you assume that.

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFF
utterances.text: Basic training, our military training suggests that we don't aim to injure people, we aim to kill people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This was inexperience.

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFF
utterances.text: I suggest it was an inexperienced firer due to the short range and the failure to hit the person directly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What you expect from a trained sniper and on the other hand, you say that he was inexperienced --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please pause after the question, for the sake of the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: JONATHAN PAUL HINCHLIFF
utterances.text: Yes, I expect a sniper to be able to engage his or her target and at that range and produce a kill. It is a medium shot range.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It is a quarter past 5.00 so we have to stop at this moment. Mr. Ierace, we will consider whether there are any further questions from the Bench tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, before you make a decision, I would be grateful for the opportunity to ask some further questions in chief in relation just to those incidents and just in relation to those aspects of those incidents, which I think will assist you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we will consider whether we come to that and certainly we will not just give a decision at this very moment. We will adjourn until 8.30 tomorrow morning same courtroom. May I ask you not to speak with anyone about the testimony until now given in this court.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. I finally, I would like to specifically express -- General Galic, I would specifically like to express the appreciation of the Chamber that you were willing to see how far we came and that you gave the opportunity to sit for such a long time today. We will adjourn until tomorrow 8.30.
